prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
The US-Iran conflict is now taking a different shape.

It began on February 28, when the United States and Israel started air strikes on Iran. The two sides agreed to a ceasefire memorandum on June 14, and the US blockade was lifted four days later. But the pause did not settle the conflict. After Iran attacked three merchant ships outside approved routes in July, the blockade restarted on July 14.

That pattern matters. The fighting is no longer only about one attack or one agreement. It is becoming a long struggle over ships, energy, and time.

Official US data show the pressure clearly. Before the war, more than 20 million barrels of oil and oil products moved through the Strait of Hormuz each day on average. In the second quarter of 2026, the average fell to 4.9 million barrels a day.

Other signs point to a longer squeeze. An opposition-media report said a petrochemical plant stopped production. It also said Iran had lost about 230 million cubic meters a day of gas production capacity since the war began. That gas figure has not been independently checked.

Diplomacy is also stuck. On August 18, President Trump said no talks with Iran were scheduled. The reported 60-day period for talks ended without an agreement. One risk group then moved its expected easing of tensions from September to the end of 2026. A news report described the region as moving back toward a dangerous and hard-to-sustain military stalemate.

This does not prove who is winning. It suggests something quieter, but important: the conflict is becoming an economic war of endurance.

【Point One】
Chris Wright said more than 17 million barrels passed through Hormuz on August 31. But that was one day. The same official data show a 4.9-million-barrel daily average in the second quarter, while a tracking service estimated about 9.1 million barrels for that day across the wider Arabian Sea, including other routes. One day alone cannot prove that Hormuz traffic has recovered. The key questions are: What was counted, where, and over what period?

【Point Two】
Ships may move more on one day while deeper damage remains. An opposition-media report described a plant shutdown and lost gas capacity. The shipping threat level remained severe because mines may still be present, no talks were scheduled, and a private risk group pushed its easing forecast to year-end. A short-term rise in shipping does not necessarily mean that industry, safe access, and diplomacy are recovering.

point_one.reasoning: 8月31日の単日データと第2四半期平均、さらに広域の推計値を区別し、数字の比較には対象範囲と期間の確認が必要だと示している。単なる免責ではなく、船舶通行の回復をどう判定すべきかという具体的な読み方を加えている。

point_two.reasoning: 単日の船舶増加が、工場停止・ガス生産能力の喪失・機雷リスク・外交停滞という深部の損傷を打ち消さないと整理している。Full Storyの個別事実を、輸送・産業・安全・外交の回復を混同してはならないという具体的な判断材料へ統合しており、新しい示唆がある。
